_about: Events between Malachi and the birth of John the Baptist, each tied to the passage where Scripture foretells or looks back on it (mostly Daniel 8 and 11). These go in the events lane. `tier`: 1 headline, 2 main, 3 detail.

events.title: Samaritans build a temple on Mount Gerizim
events.summary: The rival temple the Samaritan woman meant when she said 'our fathers worshiped on this mountain'.

events.title: Alexander conquers the Persian Empire
events.summary: The goat from the west that touched no ground: in three years Alexander of Macedon takes the whole empire of Persia.

events.title: Alexander dies; his empire is divided
events.summary: The great horn broken at its height, and four horns in its place: his generals carve up the empire.

events.title: Judea passes to the Ptolemies of Egypt
events.summary: After the battle of Ipsus, Judea is ruled from Alexandria by the 'king of the south' for a century.

events.title: The Law translated into Greek (the Septuagint)
events.summary: The Hebrew Scriptures put into Greek at Alexandria, beginning with the five books of Moses: the Bible most New Testament quotations follow.

events.title: A daughter of the south married to the north
events.summary: Ptolemy II's daughter Berenice marries Antiochus II to seal a peace; she and her child are murdered, just as Daniel 11:6 says.

events.title: Battle of Raphia
events.summary: Ptolemy IV beats Antiochus III near Gaza, but 'shall not prevail'.

events.title: Judea passes to the Seleucids
events.summary: Antiochus III beats Egypt at Panium and stands in 'the glorious land': Judea is now ruled from Antioch in Syria.

events.title: Rome defeats Antiochus III
events.summary: A commander from the coastlands puts an end to his insolence; Antiochus pays Rome tribute and dies the next year.

events.title: Antiochus IV Epiphanes takes the throne
events.summary: A contemptible person who obtains the kingdom by flatteries, and sells the high priesthood to the highest bidder.

events.title: The high priest Onias III murdered
events.summary: 'The prince of the covenant' broken: the last legitimate high priest of Zadok's line is killed.

events.title: The Temple desecrated
events.summary: Antiochus bans the Sabbath and circumcision and sets up an altar to Zeus on the altar of burnt offering: the abomination that makes desolate.

events.title: The Maccabean revolt
events.summary: The priest Mattathias and his sons, led by Judas Maccabeus, rise against Antiochus: 'the people who know their God shall stand firm and take action'.

events.title: The Temple cleansed and rededicated
events.summary: Judas Maccabeus retakes Jerusalem and rededicates the altar: the feast of Dedication (Hanukkah) that Jesus kept in Solomon's porch.

events.title: Death of Antiochus IV
events.summary: 'He shall be broken, but by no human hand.'

events.title: Judea independent under Simon the Hasmonean
events.summary: The yoke of the Gentiles is lifted: the Maccabees' family rules as priests and kings for eighty years.

events.title: Pharisees and Sadducees appear
events.summary: The two parties of the Gospels take shape under the Hasmonean kings: one devoted to the oral law and the resurrection, the other to the Temple and the written Law alone.

events.title: Pompey takes Jerusalem; Judea comes under Rome
events.summary: The Roman general settles a Hasmonean civil war by besieging the Temple Mount and walking into the Holy of Holies.

events.title: Herod made king of Judea
events.summary: Rome's senate names the Idumean Herod king of the Jews; he takes Jerusalem with Roman troops three years later.

events.title: Herod begins rebuilding the Temple
events.summary: The vast rebuilding of Zerubbabel's Temple: forty-six years in the making when Jesus first cleansed it.
